lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Magnets and Simple Machines
lesson.summary: Magnetic forces, and levers, pulleys and gears that make work easier.
learning_objectives: Test materials for magnetism and explain attract and repel
Explain that magnetic force acts at a distance
Describe how levers, pulleys and gears help us

standards.text: Compare how things move; notice that some forces need contact and some act at a distance; describe magnets as having two poles; identify magnetic materials

success_criteria: I can say which materials are magnetic
I can explain what poles do
I can name the parts of a lever
lesson.real_life: Fridge magnets, recycling centres, seesaws, wheelbarrows and bicycle gears.

warm_up.explanation: A force is a push or a pull.

blocks.markdown: Today we explore **magnets** and simple machines.
blocks.say: Welcome, young scientist! Today we test magnets, then look at levers, pulleys and gears.

blocks.alt: A magnet, an iron nail and a gear.
blocks.caption: A magnet, an iron nail and a gear.

blocks.markdown: A **magnetic** material is attracted to a magnet.
blocks.say: A magnet attracts some materials. Magnetic materials always contain a metal, but not all metals are magnetic.

blocks.alt: A pink coated paperclip on a teal felt surface
blocks.caption: A steel paperclip is magnetic.
blocks.credit: Photo by Андрей Сизов on Unsplash
blocks.say: Iron is magnetic. Steel is magnetic because it contains iron. Copper, aluminium and gold are metals, but they are not magnetic. This paperclip is steel, so a magnet would pick it up.

question.prompt: Which of these will a magnet attract?
question.explanation: A magnet attracts iron and steel.

blocks.markdown: A magnet has a north and a south **pole**.
blocks.say: A magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole. The pull is strongest at the poles.
Opposite poles attract. Matching poles repel, which means they push apart. The force acts at a distance, without touching.

scenes.caption: Opposite poles attract.
scenes.say: North meets south. The two magnets pull together.

scenes.caption: Matching poles repel.
scenes.say: North meets north. The two magnets push apart.

blocks.title: The rescue magnet
blocks.transcript: Hamza drops his steel key down a drain. How can he get it back? He ties a magnet to a string. Steel is magnetic, so the magnet attracts it. The key jumps up and sticks to the magnet. Magnetic force acts without touching. Next, a big rock blocks the path. It is far too heavy to lift. He puts a long bar on a block, the pivot. Pushing down lifts the rock. At the well, a pulley raises the bucket. The rope runs over a wheel. On his bicycle, gears turn in opposite directions to help him up the hill. Magnets, levers, pulleys and gears make life easier. No engines needed!
blocks.caption: A magnet, a lever and a pulley solve three jobs.

blocks.markdown: A **lever** turns on a **pivot**. The **load** is lifted by the **effort**.
blocks.say: A lever is a bar that turns on a fixed point called a pivot. The thing you lift is the load, and your push is the effort.

blocks.alt: A blue and yellow spring seesaw on snow
blocks.caption: A seesaw is a lever with a pivot in the middle.
blocks.credit: Photo by Luca Fabbri on Unsplash
blocks.say: A seesaw is a lever. The pivot is in the middle. Push down on one end, and the other end goes up.

scenes.caption: The pivot is the block.
scenes.say: A bar rests on a block, the pivot. A rock sits on the short end.

scenes.caption: Push here: the rock lifts.
scenes.say: Push down on the long end. The rock lifts easily. A small effort moves a heavy load.

question.prompt: In a lever, what is the load?
question.explanation: The load is what is being lifted.

blocks.markdown: A **pulley** is a wheel with a rope.
blocks.say: A pulley is a wheel with a rope. It helps you lift a load and can change the direction of your pull.

blocks.alt: Bicycle gears and a chain on a rear wheel
blocks.caption: Gear wheels on a bicycle.
blocks.credit: Photo by Wayne Bishop on Unsplash
blocks.say: Gears are wheels with teeth that fit together. Touching gears turn in opposite directions. Bicycle gears change how hard you pedal.
